title: Dumpling Dough with Boiling Water (Super)
description: This traditional "choux" pastry technique for Russian _pelmeni_ or _vareniki_ uses boiling water to partially gelatinize the starch in the flour. This process results in an exceptionally elastic and pliable dough that can be rolled very thin without tearing, ensuring the dumplings remain intact and tender during the boiling process.
instructions: Add the salt to the egg and beat with a fork. Then add 3 cups of flour and a spoonful of vegetable oil; mix well. Add 1 cup of boiling water and stir with a spoon, then knead by hand (add a little flour if necessary).
notes: *Temperature Control:* Use water that has just reached a rolling boil to ensure the flour properly scalds, which gives the dough its signature elasticity.
*Safety:* Start mixing with a spoon immediately after adding the boiling water to avoid burns; only switch to hand-kneading once the temperature is comfortable to touch.

*Resting:* Although not mentioned in the original note, allowing the dough to rest for 20–30 minutes under a bowl or plastic wrap will significantly improve its texture and make it easier to roll out.

title: Traditional Georgian Bread Shaping Instructions
description: This handwritten note outlines the manual techniques for shaping traditional Georgian dough, likely intended for _Shoti_ (long bread) or _Khachapuri_. The method focuses on preserving the dough's structure by flattening it from the center outward and keeping the edges thick, which is essential for achieving the characteristic airy crust and soft interior of authentic Georgian hearth-baked breads.
instructions: Flatten the dough by hand, starting from the center.
Leave the edges thick around the edge.
Flip the dough.
Then, flatten it lengthwise.
notes: Hand-shaping instead of using a rolling pin is vital to avoid degassing the dough completely. Leaving the edges untouched allows them to puff up during baking, creating the signature "lip" or border typical of traditional Georgian flatbreads.

title: Khachapuri Recipe by Gia Agirba
description: Imeretian Khachapuri is a cornerstone of Georgian culinary tradition, celebrated for its perfect balance of salty, crumbly Imeretian cheese and elastic Sulguni. The key to a successful khachapuri lies in achieving a high-hydration, soft dough that is handled gently to preserve its airy structure, ensuring a tender crust that complements the rich, molten cheese filling.
instructions: Dissolve yeast and sugar in warm water. Add a small amount of milk to the mixture.
Combine the liquid with the flour and salt.
Knead the dough until smooth. Add 30–40 ml of vegetable oil while kneading.
Rub a bit of oil over the surface of the dough and let it rest in a warm place until it rises.
Prepare the filling by mixing the crumbled Imeretian cheese, grated Sulguni, and eggs. Each khachapuri should contain approximately 300 g of filling.
Once the dough has risen, sprinkle flour on your workspace. Take a portion of dough for one khachapuri.
Shape and flatten the dough using circular movements.
Place the cheese filling in the center, wrap the dough around it to seal, flatten and let it rest for 10 min
Place in oven for roughly 20 - 25 minutes 200C (\~425F).
notes: *Temperature Control:* Ensure the water is lukewarm (not hot) to avoid killing the yeast; keep the rising dough in a draft-free, warm spot.
*Handling:* Use oil on your hands rather than excessive flour to manage stickiness, which keeps the dough soft and light. The dough will take roughly 40 - 45 minutes to rise.
*Cheese Ratio:* For the best results, use a 2:1 ratio of Imeretian cheese to Sulguni to achieve the traditional flavor profile and texture.
*Alternative Cheeses:* If Imeretian and Sulguni cheeses are hard to come by, you may use mexican and mazarella cheese as substitutes (respectively).

title: Vareniki Dough (Dumpling Dough)
description: This recipe utilizes the "scalded dough" technique, a staple of Eastern European culinary tradition. By pouring boiling water directly into the flour, the starches partially gelatinize, resulting in an exceptionally elastic and pliable dough that can be rolled paper-thin without tearing and maintains a silky, tender texture after boiling.
instructions: Make a well in the sifted flour.
Pour the boiling hot water into the center.
Add a teaspoon of salt and let the mixture cool slightly.
Add the oil, stir, and then add 1 or 2 eggs.
Knead the dough.
Add flour bit by bit until the dough is ready.
Combine the boiling water, oil, and salt.
Add a small amount of flour to the hot mixture to cool it down, then add the egg.
Gradually add the remaining 280–300g of flour.
Let the dough rest for 30 minutes.
notes: Ensure the water is truly at a rolling boil when added to achieve the proper "scalded" starch consistency. Always allow the hot water/flour mixture to cool slightly before adding the eggs to prevent them from scrambling. Letting the dough rest for at least 30 minutes is crucial for relaxing the gluten, making it much easier to roll out.

title: Russian Pirozhki with Scalded Yeast Dough (Yields 30)
description: This traditional recipe utilizes the "scalded" (zavarnoy) method, where boiling water is poured over a small portion of the flour to gelatinize the starches. This technique creates a dough that is exceptionally soft, easy to handle without sticking, and results in a finished pastry that stays tender and fresh much longer than standard yeast breads.
instructions: *Stage I:* Combine flour (3 tbsp), vegetable oil (3 tbsp), sugar (1 tbsp), and salt (1 tsp). Pour the boiling water over the mixture. Mix thoroughly and let it cool until it is warm to the touch.
*Stage II:* To the warm mixture, add the yeast and 1 cup of warm water. Gradually incorporate the 500g of flour. Knead the dough until smooth.

*Shaping and Cooking:* Form the dough into small balls. Let the balls rest for 5–10 minutes. Shape the pirozhki with your desired filling and fry them in a skillet with oil. Alternatively, they can be baked in the oven.
notes: The most critical step is ensuring the scalded flour mixture has cooled down to a lukewarm temperature before adding the yeast; if the mixture is too hot, it will deactivate the yeast and the dough will not rise. For a perfect fry, ensure the oil is hot before adding the pirozhki to prevent them from becoming greasy.

title: Kefir Pancakes (Blini) with Baking Soda
description: These Eastern European pancakes utilize the chemical reaction between acidic kefir (or Matsoni, a traditional Georgian yogurt) and baking soda to create a light, airy texture. Thinning the batter with milk ensures a delicate, pourable consistency typical of traditional thin blini, which are meant to be light enough to fold or roll.
instructions: Sift the flour into a bowl, then add the kefir and salt. The batter will be runny at first.
Add the baking soda and mix well with a spoon.
Gradually add more flour and mix until combined.
Add the vegetable oil and stir in.
Let the batter rest for 30 minutes.
Grease the pan with oil and cook the blini over medium heat.
notes: *Consistency:* The key to this recipe is the "liquid dough" (жидкое тесто); the batter should be thin enough to spread across the pan quickly when poured.
*Leavening:* For the best rise, ensure your kefir or matsoni is at room temperature so it reacts effectively with the baking soda.

title: Pirozhki with Scalded Yeast Dough
description: This recipe utilizes the "scalded dough" (zavarnoy) technique, where boiling water is used to pre-gelatinize a portion of the flour starch. This scientific process creates a uniquely supple and elastic dough that remains soft for several days and is particularly well-suited for deep-frying, providing a superior texture compared to standard yeast doughs.
instructions: Combine the flour, oil, sugar, and salt. Pour 1 cup of rolling boiling water over the mixture. Mix thoroughly and allow the mixture to cool.
Into the warm mixture, add the yeast and the cup of warm water. Gradually incorporate the flour in parts and knead the dough.
Form the dough into small balls and let them rest (spread) for 5 minutes.
Shape the pirozhki and fry them in a large amount of oil in a skillet.
This yields 20–30 pieces. They can also be baked.
notes: Ensure the "scalded" base from Stage 1 has cooled to a lukewarm temperature before adding the yeast in Stage 2; if the mixture is too hot, it will kill the yeast and the dough will fail to rise. When frying, maintaining a consistent medium-high oil temperature is vital for a golden-brown crust without oil-logging the interior.

title: Zeinab's Khachapuri
description: This recipe utilizes the traditional "chopped dough" technique, where butter is worked into flour to create distinct layers, resulting in a signature flaky and tender crust. The use of Matsoni (a traditional Georgian yogurt) combined with baking soda creates a light, airy rise and a subtle tang that is characteristic of authentic homemade khachapuri.
instructions: Soften the butter.
Sift 6 cups of flour and pour it over the butter.
Use a spatula to "mix" the butter into the flour.
Pour in 800g of matsoni and continue mixing.
Gradually knead the mixture until you achieve a uniform dough.
Take the remaining flour and mix it with 1 teaspoon of baking soda.
Knead and sprinkle this flour-soda mixture over it a little at a time.
Repeat the sprinkling and kneading process 3 to 4 times; do not pour all the flour-soda mixture in at once.
Form the dough into sausage shape and divide into 3 equal parts.
Store the dough in the refrigerator.
notes: *Texture Control:* When "chopping" the dough with a knife, aim for a crumbly, pea-sized texture before adding the matsoni to ensure flakiness.
*Resting:* Storing the dough in the refrigerator is essential; let it chill for at least an hour to allow the gluten to relax and the fats to firm up before rolling.

title: Adjarian Khachapuri
description: This recipe details the preparation of a traditional Georgian Khachapuri, a staple cheese-filled bread. The core science of this recipe relies on a high-hydration, enriched yeast dough that is briefly rested to develop gluten elasticity, paired with a high-heat bake (220-250°C) to ensure a rapid rise and a characteristic golden, soft crust that encases the molten cheese interior.
ingredients: Dough needs to rise at least 40 minutes
Warm water: 1/2 pitcher (300 ml water for 2 khachapuri. Add some milk)
Water: A small amount to loosen the cheese mixture
instructions: Mix the warm water, yeast, salt, sugar, and flour. Knead the dough until it is smooth and soft. Incorporate the oil at the end of kneading. Let the dough rest and rise for approximately 40 minutes.
Once the dough rises, dust the table with some flour and pinch off enough dough for one portion, about the size of a fist.
With the circular motion, round the dough into a ball, cover it up and let it rest for 10 minutes
Once rested, flatten the ball in the middle. Leave the edges thick and puffy.
Turn it over, stretch it into an oval shape. Pick it up and lay it down by folding the edges towards the center, pinch the opposite sides, creating a boat shape
Gently stretch it from the bottom towards the sides, keep shaping it like a boat
Dust some flour on the baking sheet
Add grated cheese, some sulguni on top.
Bake at 220-250 Celsius
When it's half way baked, scrape the dough off the sides with a fork
Add an egg yolk and leave in the oven for another minute
notes: *Temperature:* Ensure the oven is very hot (at least 220°C) before sliding the bread in; this high heat is vital for the dough's "oven spring."
*Texture:* The filling should be moist but not runny; add water to the cheese gradually until it reaches a spreadable consistency.
*Elasticity:* If the dough resists flattening, let it rest for 5 minutes to allow the gluten to relax.

title: Lyudmila's Beef Stroganoff
description: Lyudmila’s Beef Stroganoff reflects the historic culinary exchange between Russian and Georgian traditions. While the classic Russian dish typically features a sour cream-based sauce, this version incorporates regional Caucasian preferences for bell peppers and a tomato base, using a starch slurry to achieve the dish's signature silky consistency without heavy dairy.
instructions: Cut the meat into thin strips and flatten/tenderize each piece.
Simmer the meat in oil (with the lid off).
Add the onions, season with salt, black pepper
Add finely chopped bell peppers
Mix in grated tomatoes, tomato paste and tomato sauce
Simmer the meat again with the added ingredients.
Add a small amount of flour (half teaspoon) and stir.
At the end, prepare the thickener: dissolve 1 teaspoon of starch in a 1/2 cup of water.
Pour the mixture into the pan, slowly bring the sauce to a boil, and turn it off.
notes: To ensure the best texture, tenderize the meat thoroughly before slicing to break down fibers. When adding the starch slurry, stir constantly to prevent lumps and stop as soon as the sauce reaches a boil to maintain a glossy finish.

description: These Georgian-style meat cutlets, known as _kotleti_, are a beloved staple of Caucasian home cooking. This specific variation incorporates boiled buckwheat as a binding agent instead of the traditional heavy use of soaked bread, which introduces a deep, nutty flavor and ensures a moist, tender interior.

1/2 tsp dry spice (Khmeli Suneli), or as desired
Breadcrumbs (1/2 cup to 1 cup, or slightly more as needed)
Slightly more than 1/2 cup boiled buckwheat
instructions: The original document consists of an annotated ingredient list; specific preparation and cooking steps were not provided in the text. notes: For the best texture, ensure the boiled buckwheat is completely cooled before mixing it into the meat. Add the breadcrumbs gradually until the mixture is firm enough to hold its shape but still remains tacky to the touch.

title: Ami's Khinkali
description: Khinkali are the iconic soup dumplings of Georgia, traditionally filled with raw spiced meat that releases a rich, aromatic broth as it boils. The key to authentic flavor is the use of distinct highland herbs like blue fenugreek and summer savory, while a very stiff, cold-water dough is essential to ensure the pleats hold firm and contain the hot juices inside.
instructions: (Instructions not provided in original — combine meat filling ingredients and mix well with water or broth until soupy. Make a stiff cold-water dough, roll thin, cut circles, fill, and pleat to seal.)
notes: Ensure the dough is worked until very firm to prevent the dumplings from tearing.
When preparing the meat, mix in a small amount of water or broth to ensure a "soupy" interior once cooked.

description: This casserole version of the traditional Mexican breakfast dish relies on the corn tortillas to absorb the enchilada sauce, where the starch helps thicken the mixture and creates a cohesive, tender texture similar to a savory bread pudding or lasagna.

title: Vegetable Enchilada Casserole
description: This dish is a hearty vegetarian take on traditional enchiladas, layering classic Tex-Mex flavors into a convenient casserole format. The combination of beans, corn, and zucchini provides a satisfying texture, while layering the tortillas instead of rolling them ensures every bite is thoroughly infused with sauce and melted cheese.
instructions: Sauté onions in oil, add zucchini, beans, tomatoes, corn, cumin & salt.
Cook til hot.
In a 9×13 pan, layer in this order:
Enchilada sauce
Corn tortillas
1/2 vegetables
Cheese
Repeat — end cheese
Cover with foil.
Bake at 400°.
Bake 15 min covered, then 15 min uncovered.
notes: To ensure the casserole sets properly, make sure the vegetable mixture is steaming hot before layering.
Removing the foil for the final half of the baking time is essential for achieving a bubbly, golden-brown cheese topping.

title: Bazhe (Georgian Walnut Sauce)
description: Bazhe is a cornerstone of Georgian celebratory cuisine, prized for its rich, velvety texture and the aromatic depth provided by "Utskho Suneli" (Blue Fenugreek). Traditionally served with poultry, the sauce relies on finely ground walnuts and a precise balance of warm spices to create a creamy emulsion that characterizes the unique flavor profile of the Caucasus region.
instructions: Grind 500 g walnuts as finely as possible (pass through a meat grinder twice for best results).
Mix in 1 dessert spoon dried coriander, 1/2 dessert spoon utskho suneli, garlic to taste, chili pepper, salt, and yellow flower.
Gradually add chicken stock or boiled cooled water, stirring until the sauce reaches the consistency of heavy cream.
notes: To achieve the authentic silky consistency, walnuts must be ground as finely as possible (ideally passed through a meat grinder twice). Gradually thin the spiced walnut paste with boiled, cooled water until it reaches the consistency of heavy cream.

title: Zeinab's Shu
description: Shu is the Georgian take on French choux pastry. Light, hollow puffs filled with a rich milk-and-flour cream. Zeinab's version uses a custard-style cream thickened on the stovetop rather than a whipped filling, giving it a denser, more indulgent character typical of Georgian home baking.
instructions: Pour 1 cup of  water into a pot add salt and bring it to a boil.
Once boiling, drop in 100g of butter and bring to a slow simmer.
When butter melts, add 1 cup of sifted flour, constantly stirring on low heat
After 1-2 minutes, turn off the heat and mix in using a mixer 4 eggs
Using Nino's teas spoon, scoop 1 or 1 1/2  tsp of mixure and lay it out on a baking sheet
Heat the oven to 220 C (425 F). Once they start puffing up and rising, turn the oven down to 200 C.
And once ready, turn off the heat and leave for 3-5 minutes before removing from the oven.
Warm up milk
Separately, in a glass or bowl, mix 1 1/2 cups of sugar with 1 cup of flour.
Slowly stir in the mixture into the warming milk and whisk well. Continue on low heat until the mixture thickens and starts bubbling.
Add 50 g of butter and let simmer another 20 minutes on low heat.
Pour into a bowl and add 1 egg yolk, while the cream is hot and beat it with a mixer. (Freeze the egg whites)
From time to time, fluff the cream with a mixer (you can mix in frozen egg whites).
notes: *Cream Texture:* When making the flour slurry for the cream, ensure there are absolutely no lumps before adding it to the milk for a silky finish.
*Whipping:* For the best volume, beat the egg whites to stiff peaks before folding them into the base.

title: Czech Baklava
description: This traditional Georgian pastry, known as "Khrashuna Namtskhvari" (Crunchy Cake), relies on the reaction between _matsoni_ (Georgian yogurt) and baking soda to create a uniquely tender and crumbly shortcrust. Typically layered with a rich mixture of chopped walnuts and raisins, it represents a classic home-baking style where simple pantry staples are transformed into a textured, festive dessert often served at family gatherings.
instructions: Whisk the margarine until smooth, then add 4 egg yolks and mix well.
Combine the matsoni with the baking soda and salt, then add this mixture to the margarine.
Gradually incorporate the flour and vanilla until a soft dough forms.
Divide the dough into 3 equal portions.
Roll out each portion and sprinkle generously with a mixture of sugar, chopped walnuts, and raisins.
Layer the dough portions or roll them as desired, then brush the top with the remaining egg yolk.
Bake in a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F) until golden brown.
notes: For the most authentic "crunchy" texture, allow the dough to rest in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes before rolling.
If the dough feels too sticky, add flour gradually; the total amount needed can vary based on the moisture content of the matsoni and the size of the eggs.

title: Soft Ginger Cookies
description: These cookies achieve their signature soft and chewy texture through the combination of molasses and a specific ratio of leavening agents. The molasses provides moisture and acidity that reacts with the baking soda to create a tender crumb, while rolling the dough in sugar before baking adds a contrasting crystalline crunch to every bite.
ingredients: 1 teaspoon baking powder OR 1/2 teaspoon baking soda
instructions: Combine the first 6 ingredients.
Add this dry mixture to the creamed mixture (margarine, sugar, and egg) and molasses.
Roll dough into balls, then roll them in sugar.
Bake at 350°F for 10 minutes.
notes: Ensure your margarine and egg are at room temperature for a smooth, well-emulsified "creamed" base.
For the softest results, remove the cookies from the oven when they still look slightly underbaked in the center; they will firm up as they cool.
